chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us from Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abi al-Jarood, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far saying:
They will continue (expecting) and you will continue (expecting) until Allah sends for this matter one whom people do not know whether he has been created yet or not.

key_terms.لِهَذَا الْأَمْرِ: for this matter (referring to the Imamate or the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the state of expectation before the appearance of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir highlights the theological concept of the Imam's pre-existence in the realm of Barzakh, a key point of discussion in Shia eschatology regarding the nature of the Hidden Imam. The phrase 'whether they know he is created or not' underscores the mystery surrounding his birth and existence during the period of the Great Occultation (al-Ghayba al-Kubra), reinforcing the believers' steadfastness in anticipation despite the lack of visible proof.
